clue.text: Creature spotted around mountain slope, heading off

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the mountain's name back to front

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano, the crossword's favourite mountain

indicators.note: heading off means the word for slope loses its first letter

parts.note: the word slope taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports seeing an animal near a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna is the Sicilian volcano. 'spotted' is only a link word: the creature was seen there, so do not look for a spotted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a hoofed grazing animal, so it is an example of a creature.

clue.text: Partner in crime finished shed off, and church

indicators.note: off tells us to remove the word that precedes it

parts.note: accomplished means finished or completed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A criminal's partner finished a garden shed and the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes SHED from ACCOMPLISHED to leave ACCOMPLI.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is someone who helps another commit a crime.

clue.text: Ingredients regularly put in stewpot — not very many

indicators.note: the ingredients taken at regular intervals are every other letter

explanation.surface: A cook adds just a few ingredients to the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'stewpot' (the second, fourth and sixth) are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is a small number, just a couple, hence not very many.

clue.text: Money an accountant's invested in the neighbourhood

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A financial adviser puts cash into local businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY is British slang for money; CA stands for chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Locally means nearby, in the area close at hand.

clue.text: Harass with hurtful newspaper article

parts.note: to press someone is to harass them
cutting remarks are hurtful

explanation.surface: Someone is bullied by a nasty piece in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an article clipped from a newspaper.

clue.text: Deliberately avoid talking to one old Roman general

indicators.note: talking signals that a word is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to skip something is to deliberately avoid it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a person, perhaps a long-dead Roman commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' makes SKIP sound like SCIP. 'old' does double duty only in the surface: as wordplay it gives O, and 'Roman general' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman commander who defeated Hannibal at Zama.

clue.text: Pattern provided comfort, without question

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to cheer is to comfort

explanation.surface: Someone gave consolation without asking anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old meaning of outside, not lacking, which is what the surface wants you to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a pattern of squares, as on a chessboard.

clue.text: Hit band making old-fashioned record?

parts.note: punched means hit
a tape is a narrow band

explanation.surface: A musical group having a hit is making a vintage recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a pop band and a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: Punched tape stored data as holes in paper strip, an obsolete recording medium.

clue.text: Stone seen in ring there's nothing to be said

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

indicators.note: to be said signals a word heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A gem in a ring leaves nothing more to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be said' makes NIX sound like NYX after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Mostly irritable, note

indicators.note: mostly means almost all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: crotchety means irritable and bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone is largely bad-tempered and then a written remark follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter Y from CROTCHETY.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note worth one beat, a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: Laymen reacting in unpleasant way

indicators.note: reacting suggests a chemical change, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ordinary people respond badly to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reacting' rearranges the letters of LAYMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting meanly is behaving in a nasty or ungenerous manner.

clue.text: Parishioner curious about the origin of time becomes an expert on the past

indicators.note: about means surrounding one piece with another
curious means odd, so the letters of the word are rearranged
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchgoer interested in how time began becomes a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges PARISHIONER and 'about' puts it around T, from 'the origin of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistorian studies the period before written records, so is an expert on the past.

clue.text: Town centre and fringes of suburb lacking refinement

parts.note: the middle is the centre

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: rough means crude, lacking refinement

explanation.surface: A town's centre and outskirts are described as unpolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes of' takes the first and last letters of 'suburb', S and B. Middlesbrough is a large town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlesbrough is an industrial town on the River Tees in north-east England.

clue.text: Tennis match climax? That's not what it's said to be

definitions.text: That's not what it's said to be

parts.note: doubles is a tennis match for pairs
a peak is a climax

explanation.surface: The deciding moment of a tennis contest is misreported.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes language that means something other than it says.
explanation.definitionFit: Doublespeak is deliberately evasive or misleading language, so its words are not what they seem.

clue.text: Under wraps? Leave under wraps

indicators.note: wraps suggests folding over, so these letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret is told to stay secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'wraps' signals an anagram of LEAVE UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrevealed has not been disclosed, so it is kept secret.

clue.text: Callous yobs essentially so?

indicators.note: essentially points to letters at the core of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Are heartless thugs basically like that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' marks the letters inside 'Callous yobs'; the whole clue also asks whether such people are rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartless thugs would be thoroughly nasty, rotten in character, which is the sense meant here.

clue.text: Introduced American male — Democrat kept in check

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A US politician was brought into a meeting while being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' places D inside REIN to give REDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ushered in is to be shown in or introduced formally.

clue.text: Cold priest and bachelor face endless ordeal as unmarried men?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Eli is the Old Testament priest who trained Samuel
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a test can be an ordeal

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a single man confront a hard trial in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts TEST to TES. 'face' is a link: the priest and bachelor face the ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibates abstain from marriage, so unmarried men are examples, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Marsh bird, part gull

parts.note: a bit is a part
a tern is a seabird related to the gull

explanation.surface: A wetland bird is partly a gull.
explanation.walkthrough: A tern is not strictly a gull but close kin.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron that lives in reed beds and marshes.

clue.text: Form of transport, one from bygone era?

definitions.text: Form of transport, one from bygone era?

parts.words: Form of transport, one from bygone era?
parts.note: a horse-drawn coach running between posting stations in times past, known by a short name

explanation.surface: A clue asks about an old way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The short name for a stagecoach; 'Form' and 'era' also hint at a phase or period.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is short for stagecoach, a horse-drawn passenger vehicle of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Painter, one who's persistent, having time at last

indicators.note: at last tells us the letter goes to the end of the word

parts.note: a sticker is someone who persists

explanation.surface: An artist, a determined sort, eventually has time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having time at last' moves the T of STICKER to the end. Walter Sickert was an English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was an influential English painter of the Camden Town Group.

clue.text: Wonky centre section is fixed

indicators.note: wonky means askew, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crooked central piece has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonky' rearranges CENTRE SECTION; 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set firm and unchangeable is fixed, the idiom drawing on hardened cement.

clue.text: Dog food

explanation.surface: Food meant for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is a Chinese dog breed and also informal slang for food or grub.

clue.text: Leant over and completed cure, say

indicators.note: say signals a word heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: healed means having completed a cure

explanation.surface: Someone bent over and then got better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes HEALED sound like the sailing term HEELED.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heeled leant over to one side, the nautical sense.

clue.text: Team, one from Madrid, perhaps, involving stars

parts.note: a side is a team
Real Madrid is a football club, and Real Betis and others share the name

explanation.surface: A football side, perhaps from Spain, featuring celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests star players; Real is the club name, 'perhaps' because other Reals exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to the stars, as in sidereal time measured against them.

clue.text: Lone viewer? Yes, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase signals a word heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A solitary watcher agrees, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lone viewer' is a single organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye is one organ of sight, so a single viewer.

clue.text: English town's endless trouble with monarch

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: woe is trouble or misery
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A town suffers perpetual problems with its ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims WOE to WO. Woking is a commuter town in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Woking is a town in Surrey, England, so it is an English town.

clue.text: Plant from granny, perhaps, to small daughter

parts.note: a granny is a type of knot, hence perhaps
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Grandmother hands a plant down to a little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'granny' looks like a grandmother but is the granny knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotweed is a plant, notably the invasive Japanese knotweed.
